content.title: About
content.content: Jam or jelly, sugar free (item 5057) is a fruit spread made from fresh berries or fruits and sweetened with sugar substitutes such as stevia or erythritol. It retains the natural fruit flavor while providing low calories and a low glycemic index, making it suitable for people monitoring blood sugar levels.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sugar‑free jams often use pectin derived from apples or citrus to achieve the right thickness.
Sugar substitutes keep the product sweet without raising blood glucose.
The product can be completely vegan when it does not contain gelatin.
Without sugar as a preservative, these jams can have a longer shelf life thanks to modern packaging.
Flavor ranges from bright tart to gently sweet depending on the fruit blend and sweetener used.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: The fruits used provide vitamin C and polyphenols that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Absence of sugar makes the spread safe for diabetics and low‑carb diets.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Natural pectin acts as a soluble fiber, promoting healthy bowel movements.

items.title: Reduced calorie content
items.content: Sugar substitutes add minimal calories, aiding energy balance.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Depending on the fruit base, the jam can supply B‑vitamins, potassium and magnesium.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to specific berries or fruits used in the product.

items.title: Sensitivity to sugar substitutes
items.content: Polyol sweeteners like erythritol can cause gastrointestinal discomfort if consumed in large amounts.

items.title: High pectin content
items.content: Large amounts of pectin may interfere with the absorption of certain minerals such as iron and zinc.

items.title: Preservative additives
items.content: Some versions may contain small amounts of preservatives; people with sensitivities should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sugar‑free jam can be spread on bread, toast, crackers, used as a filling for pancakes, stirred into yogurt or cottage cheese, or incorporated into recipes that call for a sweet fruit note without added sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: After opening, keep the jam refrigerated in a tightly sealed jar. Unopened jars can be stored in a cool, dry place until the printed expiration date. Discard the product if it develops an off‑smell, mold, or unusual color.
